text: {"question":"What change in the Hubble constant is reported when the recombination history is modified by the me(z) solution compared to the standard ΛCDM prediction, and how does this compare to the H0 values obtained from the PP+DESY5 dataset in the later study?","reference_answer":"The modified recombination history leads to a higher inferred H0 from CMB data, while the PP+DESY5 analysis yields H0 ≈ 67.9 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, reducing the tension with Planck to about 2σ in the tachyon model and to 0.88σ in the dilaton model.","passage_1_contribution":"The me(z) solution produces an earlier recombination that raises the inferred H0 from CMB data.","passage_2_contribution":"The PP+DESY5 dataset gives H0 ≈ 67.9 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, lowering the discrepancy with Planck.","joint_reason":"Both passages discuss the Hubble constant, showing how different treatments of recombination or late‑time data affect its inferred value.","same_quantity":true}
